The "Vietnamization" of the Drug War; US Narco-Imperialism Goes In Search of Enemies
– The Quagmire of Tomorrow

June 2, 1998

There is nothing new about the militarization of the Drug War in DEAland. Domestic marijuana eradication has been used as an excuse for escalating the National Guard’s role in law enforcement for the better part of a decade. Outside of the US, we are slowly wading into another no-win situation that has many disturbing parallels to the situation in Southeast Asia 35 years ago.

  1. The Colombian government is losing control of more and more of the country to the control of left-wing guerrillas who are funded by the hard drug traffickers.
  2. Similarly, Mexico is being destabilized by the corruption and violence created by prohibition. The US has no higher strategic interest than the political and economic success of Mexico. Mexico will never tolerate the presence of US troops on its soil and bitterly resents the self-righteous American attitude that blames them for the consequences of our policies. On the other hand, there is a strong prohibitionist constituency in Mexico, and they show little understanding of the nature of the problem.
  3. The US military is becoming involved on the ground in Colombia and Peru, ostensibly as a part of an "anti-drug" campaign, but this inevitably involves the US in opposition to already anti-American insurgencies. It is certainly not in the US interest to have our troops involved in jungle warfare in the Andes. The situation today is remarkably similar to that in Vietnam in the early 1960’s when we only had "advisors" there. Now, as then, we have no clear strategy.
  4. Some of these radical groups may be genuine "reformers," but the Peruvian Shining Path movement is of the Khmer Rouge school. It is not in the US interest to further radicalize any of the others by being directly involved in fighting them, and Communism is no longer a global threat to the US.
  5. The US has long been identified with supporting corrupt and brutal military regimes in Latin America, because they were perceived as being anti-Communist. Just as we were ending this, we have started a second round, this time because the local military is supposedly going to help us fight "drugs." Absurdly, we are undermining democratic capitalist regimes as a part of the "Drug War" and strengthening both radical and reactionary elements that will drive more of the population to support leftist anti-democratic anti-capitalist elements.
  6. We are buying these new military allies by giving them expensive "toys" that these countries cannot afford to maintain, but which can be used against their own populations. The military in these countries will also develop strong economic incentives for prohibition through payoffs from local and international smugglers. We are undermining fragile democracies by spreading corruption.
  7. The minimum effect and primary objective of these actions is the creation of new vested interests in -- and constituencies for -- prohibition. These constituencies will then be cited as justification for expanding prohibition. This is what happened at the recent summit in Chile.
  8. The US military establishment – from the National Guard to the defense contractors – now have an enormous vested interest in prohibition. Domestically this interest is primarily in increasingly high tech equipment for population surveillance, marijuana eradication and border control. Outside of the US, it will be in supplying and maintaining low-tech equipment, at least until the war can be expanded. The Coast Guard is the victim of it own "mission creep." They are enthusiastic about the impossible.
  9. The US invasion of Panama was justified by the involvement of the Noriega regime in protecting hard drug trafficking, but after the overthrow of Noriega, trafficking through Panama increased. Noriega was actually reducing the flow by limiting it to his clients. Was the actual result of his overthrow actually the intended result? Noriega had letters of commendation from the DEA and was a (former) agent of the CIA. The Panamanians know this, even if we do not.
  10. It is worth remembering that the involvement of US government agencies and clients in hard drug trafficking began in Vietnam and continued in Nicaragua. Is there any reason to doubt that the same factors will come into play in a war that is about drug trafficking? The amount of money involved is enormous, but so are the stakes for democratic capitalism in this hemisphere.

Americans seem to think of the countries that supply us with contraband as somehow victimizing the world’s only super-power. The fact is that these countries are actually the victims of the counterproductive failure of our prohibitionism.

The US itself has been very badly damaged by prohibition, but our institutions and economy are much stronger than those of our neighbors to the south. However, if we destroy their economies and civil societies, we will not be able to isolate ourselves from the consequences. Do we really want to turn most of Latin America into one vast Vietnam on our border?

Outside of the US, we are slowly wading into another no-win situation that has many disturbing parallels to the situation in Southeast Asia 35 years ago.

However, if we destroy their economies and civil societies, we will not be able to isolate ourselves from the consequences. Do we really want to turn most of Latin America into one vast Vietnam on our border?

Any of the following stories taken by itself would be disturbing, together they create an all too clear picture of  where we going. There are many diverse interests and ideologies working here. We are far beyond just the "military-industrial complex." At this point, the political vested interest in the cover-up far exceeds the importance of all the economic interests.

The suppression of medical marijuana is the lynch pin of all of it. That is why the government has to stop it at all costs. As Solzhenitsyn said, if the lying stops the system will collapse. This is a very big system. Once the people understand the part that impacts them directly, the rest will come unraveled.

I am fully aware that the preceding paragraph sounds impossible. That is why the Internet is the only medium adequate to demonstrate the magnitude of the fine mess into which we have gotten ourselves.
